rationales: Pascal is a derived unit of pressure.
Kilogramme is an SI base unit of mass, not a derived unit.
Newton is a derived unit of force.
Watt is a derived unit of power.
Rotatory motion is the spinning of a body about its axis.
Vibratory motion is a repeated to-and-fro motion.
Circular motion is motion along a circular path, not necessarily spinning about the body's own axis.
Random motion has no fixed path or direction.
Distance is a scalar quantity.
Weight is a force and therefore has both magnitude and direction.
Mass is a scalar quantity.
Speed is a scalar quantity.
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, not the product of force and displacement.
Momentum is the product of mass and velocity.
Power is the rate of doing work.
Work is the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force.
Increasing speed does not lower a car's centre of gravity or make it more stable.
Decreasing mass alone does not ensure greater stability.
Decreasing width generally makes a car less stable.
Lowering the centre of gravity makes a racing car more stable.
Pascal’s law describes pressure transmission in a confined fluid.
Hooke’s law relates extension to applied force within the elastic limit.
The principle of floatation relates a floating body's weight to the fluid displaced.
Archimedes’ principle can be used to determine a substance’s density from its upthrust.
10⁴ N m⁻² is greater than one pascal.
10³ N m⁻² is greater than one pascal.
10⁻² N m⁻² is less than one pascal.
One pascal is equal to 1 N m⁻².
15 °C is below normal human body temperature.
37 °F is below the freezing point of water and is not normal body temperature.
98.8 °C is far above normal human body temperature.
Normal human body temperature is approximately 37 °C.
0.01 mm is typically the least count of a micrometer screw gauge, not a vernier caliper.
A typical school vernier caliper has a least count of 0.01 cm, or 0.1 mm.
1 mm is too large for the usual least count of a vernier caliper.
1 cm is too large to be the least count of a vernier caliper.
Geophysics applies physics to study the Earth, including its internal structure.
Light is a topic of physics, not the branch that studies Earth's interior.
Atomic physics studies atoms and their components.
Heat concerns thermal phenomena, not Earth's internal structure as a branch of physics.
Speed is the rate of change of distance, not displacement.
Velocity is the rate of change of displacement.
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
Deceleration is a decrease in velocity per unit time.
The SI unit of force is the newton.
The pascal is the unit of pressure.
The joule is the unit of energy and work.
The kilogram is the SI unit of mass.
Torque is the turning effect of a force.
Momentum is the product of mass and velocity.
Pressure is force per unit area.
Force alone is not the name for its turning effect.
The acceleration due to gravity at the Moon's surface is about 1.62 m s⁻².
10 m s⁻² is approximately Earth's gravitational acceleration, not the Moon's.
9.8 m s⁻² is Earth's approximate gravitational acceleration.
20 m s⁻² is far greater than the Moon's surface gravity.
Electric energy is produced when water turns turbines and generators; it is not the energy stored in the dam water.
Water stored at a height has gravitational potential energy.
Kinetic energy is associated with moving water, not water stored in the dam.
Thermal energy is not the principal energy stored in dam water.
